baseline.rule: This matrix measures the current shell against the accepted inventory; it does not recreate the inventory.
baseline.proofNotation: A proof entry is a repository path, or path::name where name is the exact node:test name or browser-guard check id inside that file; test/codex-chat-conformance.test.mjs verifies every entry resolves.

severity.highest: Can corrupt, duplicate, hide, misrepresent or prevent a normal Chat action.
severity.medium: Usable but materially below the accepted interaction quality.
severity.low: Polish or deliberately deferred breadth with a truthful fallback.

checks.requirement: Escape-first Markdown renders readable headings, lists, quotes, links and bounded code without raw HTML.
checks.beforeFinding: Headings, paragraphs, unordered lists, links and code existed; ordered lists, block quotes and code copy did not.
checks.implementation: The escape-first renderer is a line-start block parser: nested ordered and unordered lists by content indent, merged and nested block quotes that contain lists and fences, fences that only open and close at line start (an unclosed fence stays bounded code), ATX headings with closing hashes, rule precedence over list markers, and inline code spans and link hrefs held as opaque tokens so emphasis never rewrites code or mangles a URL. Every inline rule is bounded by its own delimiter, nesting depth is capped, and raw HTML is always escaped. It remains intentionally smaller than full CommonMark (no tables, setext headings or indented code) with a truthful literal fallback.

checks.requirement: Text, image and ordinary audio remain available; images paste from the clipboard, drop onto the Composer or come from the plus picker, several travel in one Turn as removable accessibly named chips; Composer grows predictably and quote context is removable. checks.beforeFinding: Attachments and audio worked, but textarea did not resize and quote context was absent.
checks.implementation: Auto-growing textarea, removable Thread-owned quote/attachment drafts and ordinary MediaRecorder flow share Turn input. File reads are rejected above 8 MiB before encoding; recording is bounded to 8 MiB or 90 seconds and announced. composer-sizing.mjs reads the computed CSS min/max-height and clamps scrollHeight inside them, so the .composer textarea rule is the single owner of the growth ceiling and the script fallback is pinned to it by test. composer-attachments.mjs takes image files from a clipboard paste or a drop (files first, file items as the fallback, image/* only) beside the plus picker, which now accepts several files; up to six attachments travel in one Turn, each refusal (count, 8 MiB byte bound, unreadable data URL) is named, chips are role=group with the attachment's name and a Remove control named for the file, and every image is sent as the image variant with a data URL (a browser File carries no filesystem path, so localImage is never produced) and renders as an image in the user message after send. composer-mentions.mjs: `@` opens a listbox fed by the host's searchFiles (debounced fuzzyFileSearch rooted at the bound repository) and `$` one fed by listSkills, both navigable with the arrow keys, inserting with Enter or Tab and closing on Escape without leaving the Composer; a pick inserts the placeholder (`@file_name`, `$skill`) and keeps a Thread-owned chip; at send each chip still present in the text is one text_elements entry whose byteRange is the UTF-8 byte span of its placeholder (TextEncoder, proven equal to Buffer.byteLength) plus one mention or skill item with the host's own name and path, and the guard driver's real-host walk reads the exact input arrays back from the fixture app-server log.

checks.requirement: A truncated event window, runtime generation change, external request resolution or runtime exit cannot leave false live state.
checks.beforeFinding: The 500-event host window had no oldest cursor/gap signal; runtimeExit and serverRequest/resolved were ignored.
checks.implementation: The host returns oldestCursor, gap, runtimeGeneration, runtimeAlive, runtimeState (alive | restarting | exited | halted) and runtimeHalt. When the app-server exits on its own, the launcher voids every pending approval or input request as requestResolved runtime_exited, respawns the process through the codex adapter client with a bounded backoff (500/2000/5000 ms), re-reads auth and the folder's Threads, resolves every Thread identity and Task link it had shown by thread/read, re-evaluates the pinned stop conditions and only then announces runtimeRestarted; a lost identity or link, three failed spawns, an unreadable account, a -32601 on a pinned request or a version/protocol mismatch halts reuse with one visible runtimeHalted and 409 runtime_halted, while the restart window answers 503 runtime_restarting. The browser drops the running posture at runtimeExit (boundary "Runtime exited during this Turn", streamed partials discarded, presence dots off), re-reads the Thread at runtimeRestarted or a generation change so thread/read is the only source of liveness, raises the persistent stop banner at runtimeHalted, removes externally resolved requests, and never claims to reconnect on its own. A bootstrap refresh no longer moves the event cursor: the stream opens at the bootstrap's cursor once and the browser's own cursor stands afterwards, so events appended between a poll and a refresh (a turn/completed, an approval request) are never dropped; the host's gap signal remains the only reason to reconcile.

checks.requirement: Submitting while one trusted Turn is live queues the message by default in the host-owned transient per-Thread queue, starts each queued message as its own turn/start with a new Turn id after turn/completed, sends nothing after turn/interrupt until an explicit Resume, and keeps steering that exact Turn available as the explicit opposite, never as the default.
checks.beforeFinding: Stop and enabled Send were simultaneous while submit always dispatched turn/start; the first repair then steered every live-Turn submission through turn/steer, unlike Codex desktop, which queues follow-ups and offers Steer per message.
checks.implementation: While a Turn streams the Send control reads Queue and Enter dispatches queueTurn into the host-owned queue (queue records come from bootstrap.queues, listQueue and the queueChanged, queuedStarted and queuedFailed host events, never from browser storage); Alt+Enter is the opposite of the label and dispatches steerTurn with the exact expectedTurnId. The queued list renders above the Composer with inline Edit (updateQueued), Delete (deleteQueued) and a per-row Steer (steerQueued with the exact expectedTurnId); the host pauses a non-empty queue on turn/interrupt and the paused copy names the host's pausedReason with Resume (resumeQueue) as the only way out; queuedStarted re-reads the Thread so the follow-up appears as its own Turn. The fixture call log proves N queued messages become N turn/start requests with distinct Turn ids, each after the prior turn/completed, in the host test and in the guard driver's real-DOM queue walk.

checks.implementation: The Chat header's title block and every Sidebar row carry a Rename control that opens an inline form (Enter saves, Escape cancels and restores focus); Save is the existing setThreadName host action (thread/name/set) and the response and the forwarded thread/name/updated both go through one handler (thread-name.mjs renameThreadRecord) that renames the list entry, the open Chat, the header, the route title and the Sidebar row, with no bootstrap refresh. The header's posture line reads the Thread's settings record (thread/start, thread/resume, thread/settings/updated) and the Permissions control offers exactly the two contract postures; Full access opens a contained alertdialog (Tab trapped, Escape and scrim close it, focus returns to the control) and only a confirmation sets the override, which travels as approvalPolicy never with sandboxPolicy dangerFullAccess on the next turn/start (Ask for approval as on-request with workspaceWrite) and is shown on that Turn's posture line.

checks.requirement: A Turn completing in a Thread off the active route, or while the window is unfocused, notifies exactly once per Turn from turn/completed through an in-app notice and the browser Notification API when permitted, governed by an Always, Only when unfocused or Never host setting that is absent after a host restart; turn/started for a Thread the Sidebar does not list refreshes the Sidebar so a brand-new Chat's first Turn shows its live dot.
checks.beforeFinding: turn/completed for a Thread other than the visible one was ignored, a brand-new Chat's first Turn showed no live dot until the periodic refresh, and a bootstrap refresh could drop events appended since the last poll.
checks.implementation: completion-notifier.mjs decides per turn/completed from the host's transient preference (bootstrap.preferences.notifications, set through setNotificationPreference, never stored in the browser): a completion the human is not looking at raises one in-app notice (toast, its own live region, a DONE badge on the Sidebar row until the Chat is opened) and, per the preference and the granted permission, one browser Notification; a bounded once-per-Turn-id dedupe makes a replayed turn/completed after a reconnect silent. Sidebar freshness (sidebar-freshness.mjs) follows the probed 0.149.0 fact that a brand-new Thread joins thread/list only once its first userMessage is durable (thread/status/changed active and turn/started in the same millisecond, the userMessage item/completed about 0.4 s later, first listed about 1.2 s after turn/started, listed idle at turn/completed): turn/started for a Thread the last bootstrap did not list keeps the browser's thread/start record as a provisional row with the live dot and arms a bounded retry (at most 4 bootstrap refreshes 750 ms apart, each scheduled after the previous settled), the refresh is keyed on that Thread's userMessage item/completed (and its turn/completed while still unlisted), a bootstrap that lists the Thread replaces the row with the host's record and ends the watch, thread/status/changed moves the row's status so the dot settles on idle, and a runtime exit ends every watch. The fixture app-server mirrors the delayed listing (CODEX_FIXTURE_LIST_NEW_THREADS=durable by default, immediate restores the old listing; CODEX_FIXTURE_USER_MESSAGE_DELAY_MS widens the window) and sends thread/status/changed in the real order, so the guard frames and the fixture lifecycle walk see a bootstrap miss the Thread before the durable cue lists it; the real-runtime lifecycle walk asserts the new Chat's own dot. A listed Thread starting a Turn is marked live and re-read once, and the event cursor is no longer moved by a refresh.
